react_result.final_narrative_text: The nine differentially abundant metabolites resolve to a chemically coherent set with no InChIKey conflicts (all nine 14-char blocks are distinct). Cross-paradigm pathway analysis identifies tryptophan metabolism as the overwhelming biological winner: it is the top-ranked pathway simultaneously in RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR = 1.50e-14, 6 hits), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p = 1.03e-06, 5 hits), and Mummichog m/z-direct activity (p = 0.0017, 8 matching compounds in the human_mfn empirical network). RaMP additionally identifies two highly specific sub-pathways — Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production (WP:WP4210, FDR = 1.10e-10) and the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR = 1.40e-08) — both enriched by quinolinic acid, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and L-tryptophan, placing the differential signal precisely along the kynurenine arm of tryptophan catabolism. Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR = 3.47e-08) captures the serotonin arm with serotonin, melatonin, and L-tryptophan as member hits. The driver metabolites span the entire tryptophan scaffold: L-tryptophan (C00078) is the entry substrate, tryptamine (C00398) and serotonin (C00780) are decarboxylation products, melatonin (C01598) is an acetyl-derivatised serotonin, quinolinic acid (C03722) and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632) are kynurenine-pathway intermediates, and 3-sulfinoalanine (C00606) reflects the cysteine-leg of tryptophan catabolism. Putrescine (C00134) is annotated separately via urea-cycle/arginine-and-proline metabolism (MUMM, p = 0.040) and likely arises from arginine decarboxylation. L-Leucine (C00123) contributes to valine/leucine degradation (MUMM, p = 0.047). The convergent signal across ORA (KEGG + WikiPathways) and m/z-direct (Mummichog) paradigms with FDR/p-value scores at or below 1e-06 on a 9-compound input constitutes strong, multi-method evidence that the treatment perturbs tryptophan metabolism at multiple branch points — both the serotonin/melatonin neuroactive branch and the kynurenine/NAD+ branch — consistent with immune activation (IDO induction) or indoleamine-2,3-dioxygenase activity.
